title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization
claim: A frozen generative model plus differentiable evaluators lets gradients flow end-to-end through sampling to optimize the conditioning signal at test time.
layout: 5 boxed stages, left-to-right with bottom feedback loop, color-coded gradient arrows and legend
description: A dense system diagram with five numbered, color-coded boxes. A noise input sits at the top. Box 1 (blue/green) lists fixed and optimizable conditioning variables with small icons. Box 2 (purple) is the frozen diffusion proposer. It shows the classifier-free guidance equation and a row of circles for the DDIM chain x_T to x_0, with a dashed arrow beneath it and a note that the sampler is differentiable. Box 3 (blue) is the frozen surrogate evaluator. Box 4 (red) is the physics-informed loss, with a sum formula and four icons for performance, constraints, physics and regularization. Box 5 (orange) runs along the bottom as a right-to-left loop: backpropagation, gradients, optimizer, then update of c_opt, which feeds back to Box 1. A legend at lower right separates forward pass, gradient flow, optimization update and frozen modules. Solid black arrows show the forward path and dashed purple and green arrows show the backward path.
caption: Overview of D2C. A frozen conditional diffusion proposer generates designs from conditioning inputs, a frozen surrogate evaluator and physics-informed penalties define a differentiable test-time objective, and gradients are backpropagated through the deterministic DDIM chain to optimize the conditioning signal. Multiple noise trials and loss-weight samples produce a candidate pool, from which the best valid design is selected after domain-specific constraint checks.
abstract: Optimizing high-dimensional physical systems under expensive evaluations and complex constraints is a central challenge in science and engineering. In offline model-based optimization (MBO), methods must improve designs using only a fixed dataset and no test-time access to the true objective. However, existing methods typically suffer from conservatism, unconstrained surrogate exploitation, or function as static inference-time samplers that cannot refine candidates against precise physical objectives. In this paper, we propose Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning (D2C) for offline MBO, which leverages the fact that deterministic sampling makes the reverse denoising chain differentiable with respect to the conditioning signal. D2C turns a frozen conditional diffusion model into an end-to-end gradient-based optimizer by directly optimizing conditioning variables at test time via gradients from frozen surrogate objectives and physics-informed penalties backpropagated through the reverse chain. We implement this idea in a composed proposer-evaluator framework and evaluate it on laser pulse optimization for inertial confinement fusion, sustainable data-center workload scheduling, and four Design-Bench tasks. Our method achieves the strongest results on the two real-world tasks and the best average rank across four Design-Bench tasks.
